verdicts.note: S9 records his vote for a 0.1% city sales tax to house people who are homeless and fund their services, and S1 lists affordable housing among his goals. Both are public investment in housing, pole_b. A single vote plus a platform line supports +1 at medium, not more. No rent-regulation or tenant-protection position is recorded.
One recorded vote for a new local tax (S9). Magnitude 1 at medium matches the single-vote rule, and nothing else in the dossier speaks to taxes.

Attacked as aspirational. S1 and S2 list goals (living wages, child care, elder care, security from medical bankruptcy) without naming county programs or budgets, and the scoring does not cite S10's $20,000 Community Lifeline grant. Still, the statement explicitly calls for government to deliver these programs. That is a single clear statement, so +1 at medium holds.

The evidence is indirect: shelter funding and a homeless-services tax (S9, S10), and a motion to pause the Flock camera contract (S12). They lean toward services and limits on surveillance, but he states no policing platform. Low confidence is the right level; the app excludes low scores from alignment math.
Second-term Shelton council member (S7, S8) running on that record, new to county office. -1 at medium is consistent with Blush's -1.

S1 and S2: he would unite code enforcement with the Sheriff's Office against encampments, dumping and blight, and he cites 'cracking down on crime and encampments.' Clearing encampments is named in pole_a. Repeated, explicit platform language supports -2. Medium confidence (pamphlet only, no recorded vote) is appropriately cautious.

The evidence is one generic line, 'ending wasteful spending and living within our means,' plus 'promoting fiscal responsibility' and opposing garbage rate hikes (S1, S2). Pole_a is audits, oversight and performance standards before any new spending. The dossier records no audit proposal, named cut or budget vote. Compare Duenkel (-2, high) in the auditor race, who has a record of audit demands and cut his own office's budget. A lean toward restraint is supported; full pole_a is not.
One recorded vote against a new local sales tax (S6), so magnitude 1 at medium. Opposing garbage rate hikes (S1) is about a utility rate, not a tax, so it does not raise the magnitude.

He runs explicitly on 'proven government, business, and nonprofit leadership experience' (S1). He has been on the council since 2024 (S5) and chairs the housing authority and the park board. -1 at medium holds.
